findings.claim: The lab/day timing is not yet demonstrably honest. The intake assigns the collections-in-depth module lab to all three F25 coding-capable Concept blocks (12 + 20 + 40 = 72 minutes), while the five F25 topic pages total 56 minutes. Those allocations total 128 minutes before any explicit account of overlap, exceeding the frozen 120-minute day, yet line 155 concludes that day totals fit by counting topic pages only. The planned labs also have no minute estimate, so a learner workload cannot be checked without double-counting blocks.

evidence.section: Frozen dayTypes.Concept, dayTypes.Practice, and dayTypes.Review block definitions; canonicalized selected JSON text

findings.recommendation: Add planned minutes for each module lab and a mutually exclusive day-block allocation showing which topic-page minutes and lab minutes satisfy each F25-F27 activity. Do not compress honest topic budgets; narrow or integrate lab work as needed so every minute is counted once and each day remains at or below 120 minutes.

findings.claim: The blueprint declares six coding objectives covered by only two 15-minute tasks, but its learner-facing task descriptions do not elicit all six. In particular, big-o-basics#o3 requires rewriting a nested-loop lookup and stating complexity before and after; neither 'collections and equality' nor 'sorting and grouping using streams' commits to that performance rewrite. The current blueprint therefore overstates direct objective coverage, and the feasibility of assessing three distinct objectives per short task is not evidenced.

evidence.section: Why should assessments, learning objectives, and instructional strategies be aligned?

findings.recommendation: Map each of the two coding tasks explicitly to the operations it elicits. Either require the nested-loop rewrite and before/after complexity statement in a task and validate that the complete task fits 15 minutes, or remove big-o-basics#o3 from this blueprint's coding coverage while retaining representative course coverage. Apply the same direct-evidence check to the other five coding objectives without changing the fixed 45-minute block or the frozen formats.

findings.claim: Objective o1 is not unambiguously observable as written. Whether a Set or Map keeps insertion or sorted order depends on the concrete implementation, and 'duplicates' means elements for a Set but keys versus values for a Map. A learner can give different correct answers without a named implementation and a statement of what is duplicated.

evidence.section: Unmodifiable Sets: iteration order is unspecified
Map encounter order varies by implementation

findings.recommendation: Rewrite o1 to predict duplicate handling and encounter order for given named implementations and code, explicitly distinguishing duplicate map keys from duplicate values. Keep the existing List/Set/Map syllabus scope; only make the conditions and expected evidence precise.

findings.claim: The F28 review asks learners to diagnose ConcurrentModificationException, but no F25-F27 objective commits to teaching or practising that concept. The intake simultaneously states that F28 review topics contain no new syllabus. The other o3 diagnoses are traceable to prior objectives; this one currently risks first exposure during retrieval practice.

evidence.section: Class description and fail-fast iterator behavior

findings.recommendation: Either make prior teach-then-do coverage of iterator modification and ConcurrentModificationException explicit under the existing 'Lists, sets and maps in depth' topic before F28, or replace this review diagnosis with a bug already guaranteed by an earlier objective. Do not introduce the concept for the first time in the review.
